G-protein-coupled receptors constitute one of the major signal transduction systems in eukaryotic cells.  Coding sequences for these receptors, in those regions believed to contribute to the agonist-antagonist binding site, are strongly conserved across mammalian species. Chemokine CCR1 to CCR6 receptor agonism appears to be involved in the selective accumulation of leukocytes in inflammed tissue, and in the pathogenesis of inflammatory and autoimmune diseases.
